title: Toki
build: Ocean type 1 cartridge, 16 banks of 8 KB (128 KB)

records.c: The first 11 bytes of Stage 3's data block, loaded from $0C01. Bytes 2-4 are the stage's three background colours ($D021-$D023; stage_setup_tables copies them to bg_colour0-2): 00, 0E, 08 here. Byte 5 (09) is the number of the last section, which track_stage_section and init_round_state read. Bytes 6-7 ($8827) point into cartridge bank 0 to the 64 bytes of stream records that load_stage_bank_records copies to $0100. Bytes 8-9 ($8940) point to the list of animation ids that the helper at $06E6 searches, and byte 10 (48) is that list's last index. Bytes 0 and 1 (69, 57) are read by nothing in play.

The 22 bytes $0C0C-$0C21 are Stage 3's eleven table pointers; stage_setup_tables copies them to $2A-$3F (map_row_lo_ptr, map_row_hi_ptr, block_chars_ptr, block_props_ptr, path_table_ptr, $34, script_ptr_a, script_ptr_b, anim_lo_ptr, anim_hi_ptr and $3E). Their values here are $1C1E, $1C75, $0D36, $1BD4, $1DC5, $2075, $2304, $2341, $22AC, $2263, $22F5.

Colour of each character code in Stage 3, 256 bytes, indexed by the character (screen code) found in the screen buffers. recolour_screen copies the entry for every one of the 840 playfield characters into colour RAM. Only the low nibble reaches colour RAM, and a value of 8 or more turns on multicolour for that character, since the playfield runs in multicolour text mode ($D016 bit 4).

Table of section record addresses for Stage 3: one word for each of its 10 sections, $0D22-$0D35, starting $1CCC, $1CE5, $1CFE and on, each 25 bytes on. store_section_index indexes it with section_index times 2, track_stage_section with the next and the previous section's index times 2, and init_round_state with the last section's ($0C06); stage_setup_tables reads the first word through $24.

The map block table of Stage 3: four screen characters for each of 74 block numbers (upper left, upper right, lower left, lower right), $0D36-$0E5D, pointed to by block_chars_ptr ($2E). The table's length depends on the stage.

The block numbers of Stage 3's map, one byte for each block position, from $0E5E to $1BD3. map_row_lo/hi_table give each of the 87 rows' start (first $0E50, $0E79, $0EA2); rows differ in length, and a row's pointer is biased by the row's first column, so the byte for block column x is at the row pointer plus x. Each byte indexes block_chars and block_props_table.
Bytes $125E-$165D of map_rows_data ($125E is 1024 bytes in).
Bytes $165E-$1A5D of map_rows_data ($165E is 2048 bytes in).
Bytes $1A5E-$1BD3 of map_rows_data ($1A5E is 3072 bytes in).

Map block properties of Stage 3, one byte for each block number: 74 bytes $1BD4-$1C1D, matching the 74 four-character blocks of block_chars ($0D36-$0E5D). block_props_ptr ($30) points here. Bit 0 solid, bit 1 harmful, bits 2 and 3 slopes, bit 5 enter mode 1, as block_property_at and the terrain probes test them. The values present are $00, $01, $03, $04, $05, $08, $09, $10, $11.

Map row address table, low bytes: 87 entries $1C1E-$1C74, one for each row of Stage 3's map. map_row_lo_ptr ($2A) points here and stage_setup_tables copies the pointer from $0C0C. The high bytes are the 87 bytes at $1C75.

Map row address table, high bytes: 87 entries $1C75-$1CCB. map_row_hi_ptr ($2C) points here and stage_setup_tables copies the pointer from $0C0E. The low bytes are map_row_lo_table at $1C1E; a row starts at hi:lo.

The 10 section records of Stage 3, 25 bytes each, $1CCC-$1DC5: section_table ($0D22) holds their addresses. Each record begins with the follow zone (zone_left, zone_right, zone_top, zone_bottom) and the view limits that update_view_scroll reads through section_ptr ($26), and holds the flags byte at offset $16 (section_scroll_flags); the rest of the 25 bytes is not decoded here. Four fields are rewritten at the start of a round: stage3_patch sets bytes 10-13 of section 2 ($1D08-$1D0B, the smallest and largest view_top) to $00A0 and $00A0 when the round starts in a section below 2, and the handler at $A7F3 (entry 7 of the obj_flags handler table at $A868, not the obj_kind type-7 handler $A96D) later widens them to $0140 and $01F0; stage3_common clears bytes 8-9 of section 6 ($1D6A-$1D6B, the largest view_left). Bytes 6-13 of a record are the view limits: smallest and largest view_left, then smallest and largest view_top, a word each.

Table of path data addresses that path_table_ptr ($32) points to, indexed by obj_arc_state; the pointer is one below the first entry in the stage 1 table, so the table's first word may start at $1DC6. The pointer at $34 is $2075. The area from $1DC6 to $2074 is 687 bytes; the format of its words is as in stage 1's path_address_table.

The table the pointer at $34 (a copy of $0C16, here $2075) points to: script command 22 ($B722) reads it through ($34) at $B72D to find the record of an object it sets up. In stage 1 the first path data and these records lie together in this area; where this stage's path data ends is not established.

High bytes of the addresses of Stage 3's animation data blocks, 73 entries $2263-$22AB indexed by animation number; anim_hi_ptr ($3C) points here. The low bytes are the 73 bytes of anim_lo_table at $22AC.
Low bytes of the addresses of Stage 3's animation data blocks, 73 entries $22AC-$22F4, indexed by animation number; anim_lo_ptr ($3A) points here. The partner of anim_hi_table.

The eleventh table of Stage 3, which $3E points to (stored by stage_setup_tables from $0C20): the hit reactions 0 and 1 ($A8FA, $A8D8) replace an object's obj_anim_num with the entry at that index, so it maps an animation number to the animation the object switches to when hit. It starts at $22F5.

Low bytes of the addresses of Stage 3's object movement scripts: 61 entries $2304-$2340, the table that script_ptr_a ($36) points to. object_script_step loads the pair (script_ptr_a, script_ptr_b) into $E3/$E4 and then reads the script byte at ($E3) + obj_script_pos ($379C,x). The high bytes are script_addr_hi.
High bytes of the addresses of Stage 3's object movement scripts: 61 entries $2341-$237D, the table that script_ptr_b ($38) points to; the low bytes are script_addr_lo.

Object movement script bytes of Stage 3, from $237E; the scripts start between $237E and $26EF. A byte below $80 is a command number: object_script_step looks it up in script_cmd_lo/hi at $B33C/$B35F and runs it; a byte with bit 7 set is a move (low four bits the direction, next byte the repeat count).
Bytes $277E-$27CC of script_data ($277E is 1024 bytes in).

Stage 3 entry for table indexes 6, 10, 20, 21 and 25. When obj_off_y,x and obj_speed,x are both non-zero it tests whether $E7/$E8 is at most player_box_right ($4E/$4F) + $10, and when that holds on every 4th frame (frame_count & 3 is zero) decrements obj_speed,x. When obj_off_y,x is zero it skips that test; when obj_speed,x is zero it skips the x move. Otherwise it subtracts obj_speed,x from the position $E7/$E8, and jumps to resident object_reset_motion ($A8E0) once $E9/$EA reaches $0538 or more, otherwise returns. Entries 22 ($BD86) and 26 ($BD84) are not routine starts in this stage: $BD84 is the operand of the adc at $BD83 and $BD86 the operand of the sta at $BD85.

Stage 3 entry for table index 19. A phase state machine for one object, driven by obj_arc_state,x and the state bytes at $BFFE-$C007 (set up by stage3_tail, see stage3_runtime_state_bytes). If obj_arc_state,x is 0 it jumps to stage3_idle_countdown; otherwise it calls $B5D5 and, when bit 6 of obj_arc_state is set, rewrites bytes at $30CA-$30F2 (animation data, not code) and probes block_property_at (a=$24, y=$54); if that is non-zero it clears obj_arc_state,x, sets $E9/$EA=$04FE and, when bit 0 of $C002 is set, counts $C004 down and on zero takes the next entry of stage3_pattern_table_b ($BFF3, index $BFFF wrapping at 7) and sets $C000, $C006, $C007 to 3; when bit 0 is clear it stores 0 in $C000. Falls to stage3_spawn_check when bit 6 is clear. Entries 9 ($BDE0), 27 ($BE34), 29 ($BE2E) and 30 ($BE31) start instructions inside this routine and 7 ($BE73) one inside stage3_spawn_check, so none is a routine start; 23 ($BE91) and 28 ($BE8D) point into operands.

Branch target of stage3_state_machine_step when bit 6 of obj_arc_state is clear. If obj_arc_counter,x equals $14 it patches $30CA/$30D6, increments $C005, loads $3418 from stage3_value_table indexed by $C005 & 3, copies the position $E7-$EA into the slot-4 position arrays ($393A, $3997, $39F4, $3A51) and sets $3FC4=$18, $352F=4, then continues into the common slot set-up at $BEBF. Otherwise returns.

Reached only from stage3_idle_countdown (the bpl at $BEF2, with y = $C006). The branch of stage3_state_machine_step to $BE89 does not get here: it stores 6 in $C000 and returns at $BE8E. Decrements $C006 and sets $C000 to 3 (still non-negative) or $19, sets $3FC0,y=$30, then fills slot y of the object arrays based at object 74: position bytes at $3936, $3993, $39F0 and $3A4D from $E7-$EA plus $0A and $0E, and at $BEBF the fixed values in $35DC, $3639, $3696, $3F63, $3318, $3F06, $3C7B and $3D35, plus $14=$4A. This looks like spawning a projectile or part object (probably). Ends with rts at $BEE9.

Reached by jmp from stage3_state_machine_step when obj_arc_state,x is 0. Decrements $C000 and returns while it stays non-negative; otherwise reads $C006 and branches to stage3_spawn_shot if non-negative. If $C007 is set it puts back $BD, $B7, $BC at $30DA, $30CA, $30D6 (bytes of Stage 3's animation data, the values stage3_tail stores), sets $C000=6 and clears $C007; if not, it continues into stage3_phase_select.

Continuation of stage3_idle_countdown. Tests bit 0 of $C002; if set it steps through stage3_pattern_table_a using the index in $BFFE (wrapping at 7) and the counter in $C003, and sets obj_dir,x to 7 or $0B, and stores $C1/$C6 at $30E2/$30EE (animation data); if clear it stores $C3/$C7 at $30EA/$30F2 and sets $C000=$19. Either way it ends by setting obj_arc_counter,x ($20 or 8), setting obj_arc_state,x=$80, flipping obj_dir,x with eor #$0C, and decrementing $C002. $BF22-$BF25 carry the resident names stage4_bf22..stage4_bf25 (the bytes stage4_patch writes for Stage 4); in Stage 3 they are ordinary instruction bytes.

Stage 3 entry for table index 16. Calls $B5D5, then if obj_flags bit 4 is clear it probes block_property_at (a=$0C, y=$15). With obj_arc_state,x = 0 and the probe bit 0 clear it sets obj_arc_state,x=$C0 and obj_arc_counter,x=1. With obj_arc_state non-zero and probe bits 0-1 set it decrements obj_motion_alt,x; when that goes negative it snaps $E9 to a grid of $10 (offset $15) and sets obj_flags bit 4 and clears bit 5, otherwise it clears obj_arc_state,x.

Stage 3 entry for table index 17. Decrements obj_off_y,x and returns while non-zero. When it reaches zero it reloads obj_off_y,x=$50, compares player_box_left ($4C/$4D) with $E7/$E8, stores $33 in obj_motion_alt,x when player_box_left is below $E7/$E8 and $34 otherwise, and jumps to resident $4C9D (the trigger that swaps obj_motion and obj_motion_alt).

Data, 7 bytes ($BFEC-$BFF2): values read as $BFEC,y in stage3_idle_countdown's continuation, where y comes from $BFFE and wraps at 7. The result is stored into $C003 (bit 7 added for the second pass). The disassembly shows jam/ora here but these are data.
Data, 7 bytes ($BFF3-$BFF9): values read as $BFF3,y in stage3_state_machine_step with y from $BFFF (wrapping at 7), stored into $C004.
Data, 4 bytes ($3F,$40,$41,$42) read as $BFFA,y in stage3_spawn_check, indexed by $C005 & 3, and stored into $3418. The disassembly shows these as rla/jam but they are data.

One Field of ten bytes ($BFFE-$C007): the last bytes of Stage 3's code load (directory entry 24, $BD76-$C007, which also covers the first eight bytes of the character set). stage3_tail ($4E7D) resets them at the start of each round ($FF, $00, $00, $00, $01, $80, $06, $FF, $FF, $00), and the stage code reads and writes them as state (indexes at $BFFE/$BFFF, flags and counters at $C000-$C007). $C008 starts stage_charset.

The character set of the playfield for Stage 3, $C008-$C477: directory entry 23 copies 1144 bytes to $C000-$C477, and the stage code (entry 24, to $C007) then covers character 0, so the set as used starts at character $01. Eight pixel rows for each character (VIC bank 3, $D018 $21 or $31). stage_load copies it from the cartridge at stage start.
Bytes $C408-$C477 of stage_charset ($C408 is 1024 bytes in).
